stories.headline: A Learjet bound for the Bahamas nose-dives onto a Palm Beach County road, killing all nine people aboard
stories.summary: All nine people on a Learjet 60 died Sunday afternoon when the jet slammed into a roadway near the Cresthaven neighborhood of Palm Beach County, Florida, a few miles from Mar-a-Lago, around 12:50 p.m. The flight had left Austin, Texas, for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. Dashcam video shows the jet diving nose-first into the road and exploding, leaving a burning crater. In air traffic control audio, a pilot first reports "light, clear ice" and moderate turbulence, then calls "Mayday" while descending 10,000 and then 20,000 feet per minute. Gov. Ron DeSantis said it "looked like a missile going down"; debris hit nearby homes, but no one on the ground was reported hurt. About 600 mobile-home residents were evacuated. The FAA and NTSB are investigating, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called it a horrific tragedy.

stories.headline: Two days before Election Day, Democrat Haley Stevens shocks her party by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers for Senate in Michigan
stories.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost Michigan's Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed in August, endorsed Trump-backed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday after attending a Detroit church service with him. She said El-Sayed's campaign had uninvited her from a joint event that same day: "Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away. And he's right. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers." Her top aide quit over the move. Tensions had simmered since the primary; Stevens is a strong supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a sharp critic who has drawn fire for past remarks and appearances with streamer Hasan Piker. El-Sayed brushed it off, saying "I actually don't think about Haley Stevens." President Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson later invited her to join the GOP. The seat, held by retiring Democrat Gary Peters, is key to Senate control.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: Election Day Tuesday, curbside leaf pickup starts Wednesday, and a new pumpkin drop-off at the transfer station
stories.summary: Trumbull votes in Tuesday's state election (polls are open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.); polling places by district are listed in the town clerk's warning along with sample ballots, and absentee ballots are counted at the Trumbull Library on Quality Street. Public Works expects the town's loose-leaf pickup to begin Wednesday and run until every neighborhood is done, with a progress map updated daily; bagged pickup can be requested anytime, and pumpkins left with leaf piles will be collected too (questions: 203-452-5070). A new pilot lets residents drop undecorated pumpkins in a marked dumpster at the transfer station from Nov. 2 to 20. Wednesday night, the Zoning Board of Appeals hears a height variance for a gymnasium at 2320 Huntington Turnpike, and the Town Council gets a Hillcrest Middle School building update and honors the Middlebrook School Odyssey of the Mind team.

stories.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy is hospitalized after a stroke at his son's hockey game; his office expects a full recovery
stories.summary: Connecticut U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy, 53, suffered a stroke Saturday afternoon after feeling numbness in his arm while at his son's hockey game, his office said Sunday. He was taken to a local hospital, where doctors found the stroke, and was then transferred to Johns Hopkins for monitoring. Chief of staff Allison Herwitt said he is responding well to treatment, is awake and alert, and that doctors are optimistic he will make a full recovery. Murphy is not on Tuesday's ballot but had spent recent weeks campaigning in Connecticut and swing states and was due in New Hampshire on Sunday. Rep. Jahana Hayes shared the news at a Meriden canvass launch, where volunteers gasped.

stories.headline: Jets score on their first six drives and still lose 38-33 to the Raiders, falling to 2-6
stories.summary: The Jets blew a 23-14 halftime lead and a 30-21 third-quarter lead and lost 38-33 to the Las Vegas Raiders at MetLife Stadium on Sunday. New York scored on its first six possessions for the first time since 2008, and Braelon Allen ran for a career-high 147 yards on 21 carries, including a 21-yard touchdown, while Adonai Mitchell posted a career-high 142 receiving yards and a score. Geno Smith went 22-of-30 for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. But Kirk Cousins threw three touchdown passes, and back-to-back Raiders scoring drives, set up by a 45-yard Ashton Jeanty catch-and-run, gave Las Vegas the lead for good. The Jets outgained the Raiders 439-333 and still dropped another one-score game. "It's an understatement to say we're all disappointed," coach Aaron Glenn said. Next up: the Chiefs.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli, 20, clinches the F1 title in Mexico and becomes the youngest world champion ever
stories.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli wrapped up the 2026 Formula 1 world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix on Sunday with four races still left, becoming the youngest champion in the sport's history at 20. He finished third, enough to knock his last rivals out of mathematical contention, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record (Vettel was 23 in 2010). Antonelli, in only his second F1 season, has won nine of 19 races and is Italy's first world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Max Verstappen won the race and Lewis Hamilton, who started on pole, was second, so Antonelli shared the podium with two legends. Teammate George Russell, the preseason favorite, finished sixth after a 10-second penalty for a crash. "I'm speechless," Antonelli said.

stories.headline: Hackers push fake nuclear and radiation alerts to Ukrainians' phones, and Russia says its own alert app was hit hours later
stories.summary: Late Sunday night Ukrainians got a wave of false alerts on the country's Air Alert app warning of radiation hazards, chemical threats and street fighting, and telling them to stay indoors. One message, in Russian, claimed all of Ukraine was under nuclear alert and added "Don't worry, Oreshnik is in action," referring to Russia's nuclear-capable hypersonic missile. Ukraine's Air Force said the app had likely been "compromised by the enemy" and that there was no radiation threat; the developers temporarily shut it down. A pro-Kremlin Telegram channel said a group called Hitcorecorp claimed responsibility, which NBC could not verify. Hours later Russia said its own alert system had been hacked. The dueling claims came as the short Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire ended, raising fears of heavier fighting.

stories.headline: An American EWTN executive becomes the first laywoman to run a Vatican ministry, taking over all its media
stories.summary: Maria Montserrat "Montse" Alvarado, a 39-year-old Mexican-born American who has been president and COO of EWTN News since 2023, starts this week as head of the Vatican's communications department, the first laywoman to lead a Vatican "ministry" and the first non-Italian to run it. The department oversees the Vatican's TV, radio and print outlets and its press office. Analysts say the pick shows that American-born Pope Leo XIV sees women's roles differently than his predecessors, since senior women at the Vatican have usually been nuns. Alvarado said she never applied: "It was an appointment from the Holy Father." EWTN, the largest Catholic TV network in the U.S., is a touchstone for conservative Catholics, and some of its shows were sharply critical of Pope Francis.

stories.headline: Halloween weekend shootings in nightlife districts and college towns leave at least 6 dead and dozens hurt
stories.summary: Mass shootings in nightlife areas across the U.S. over Halloween weekend killed at least six people and injured dozens, officials said. The worst was in Dallas, where three shootings in about 75 minutes Saturday night in the Deep Ellum entertainment district killed four and wounded 15, despite extra police on patrol; some arrests were made. In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight wounded in two shootings outside Legion Field after the Magic City Classic between Alabama State and Alabama A&M, which drew nearly 70,000 fans; one person was detained and multiple weapons were found. Six people were shot near the University of Delaware campus in Newark, and police in Fayetteville, Arkansas, and Bloomington, Illinois, also reported shootings in their bar districts.

stories.headline: Utah teen Kylie Arellano is found safe in Oregon after more than 500 days missing; a 39-year-old man is in custody
stories.summary: Kylie Arellano, who vanished from her family's home in Garden City, Utah, on May 29, 2025, when she was 15, was found safe in Oregon on Sunday, ending a search that stretched more than 500 days. Oregon officers working with the FBI's Salt Lake City field office and the Rich County Sheriff's Office recovered the now-17-year-old, who was with a 39-year-old man; he was taken into custody without incident. Investigators had chased dozens of unconfirmed sightings across the U.S. and abroad. FBI Director Kash Patel said local police acted on information from the Salt Lake City office, and the FBI said no more details will be released while the case is ongoing. Oregon State Police, the FBI's Portland office and Utah public safety officials also helped.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo owners find they can't change Display Zoom after setup; Apple Support says erasing the phone is the only fix
stories.summary: Some iPhone Duo owners have discovered that Apple's first foldable lacks the Display Zoom setting that normally lives under Settings > Appearance. On every iPhone, setup asks you to choose how big text and icons look (Default, Medium or Large), and you can usually change that later. On the Duo the option is missing, so you're stuck with whatever you picked during setup. A Reddit user spotted it last week, and a MacRumors forum member says an Apple senior support advisor told them the only way to change it is to erase the phone and set it up again. MacRumors confirmed the option is still missing on the latest iOS 27.2 and has asked Apple about it. Worth knowing before you restore or set up a Duo.

stories.headline: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pros, an OLED iPad mini and an M6 iMac all go on sale this Friday
stories.summary: Five new Apple products that opened for pre-order last week launch Friday, Nov. 6: an iPad mini with an OLED display and A20 Pro chip (from $699), an iMac with the M6 chip (from $1,499), a 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 (from $1,999), and Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pros with OLED displays in 14-inch ($2,899) and 16-inch ($3,399) sizes. All five are still available to pre-order, and most configurations show launch-day delivery. The exception is the base 14-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro: Space Black is quoted at 3 to 4 weeks and silver at 7 to 10 business days. Apple also reports its fiscal fourth-quarter results today, Nov. 2.

stories.headline: Bruce Dickinson says the first single from his new AI-free solo album arrives within two weeks
stories.summary: Iron Maiden singer Bruce Dickinson told Chile's Radio Futuro on Sunday that the first single from his eighth solo album will be out within the next two weeks, with the album due in early 2027 on BMG. Most of it was recorded last January and February at Dave Grohl's Studio 606 in California with producer Brendan Duffey, who also mixed it, as the follow-up to 2024's The Mandrake Project. Dickinson repeated that it was made without artificial intelligence and without samples: "A.I. is not creative. All it does is copy... A.I. is just stealing your creativity and chucking it back at you with no soul." He said the band worked 12-hour days for three weeks and cut 18 songs, so many that some were left off to avoid a double album.

stories.headline: Metallica mark Halloween at the Las Vegas Sphere with 'Of Wolf and Man' and an Addams Family jam
stories.summary: Metallica celebrated Halloween at their Las Vegas Sphere residency on Oct. 31 by pulling out "Of Wolf and Man," the Black Album deep cut, for the first time at the Sphere (and the first time anywhere since their July 3 London Stadium show). James Hetfield told the crowd to "seek the wolf in thyself" as the screens showed a blood-red sky and a giant bronze door carved with the band members' heads. The set opened as usual with "Blackened," "Fuel" and "Leper Messiah." For their nightly "Kirk and Rob Doodle," Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo, wearing a bright red wig, mashed up "I Disappear" with the theme from The Addams Family. Fan-shot video of both is in the story.

stories.headline: Pedal Pawn's first wah, the Say Wah, took six years to build and chases the SRV and Hendrix sound
stories.summary: British pedal maker Pedal Pawn, known for gear aimed at Stevie Ray Vaughan and Jimi Hendrix fans (it once tracked down SRV's own TS9 to reverse-engineer its BluesPrint overdrive), has launched its first wah pedal, the Say Wah, named after the opening track of SRV's 1985 album Soul to Soul. Founder Chris King Robinson, who started the company in his mother's garage in 2019, says the first concept dates to 2020 and it's the longest he has spent on any product. After owning hundreds of wahs, he says most have either great midrange "quack" or a great sweep but miss the vocal top end. His goal was the classic sound "most people hear in their head when you say 'wah pedal,'" built from scratch rather than cloned.

stories.headline: LEGO Insiders Weekend is Nov. 21-22, and this year the deals reportedly end before Black Friday
stories.summary: Early rumored details on LEGO Insiders Weekend 2026, via BrickTap, point to a change from past years: the sale reportedly ends the day before Black Friday instead of running through Cyber Monday. Double Insiders points, worth about 10% back to spend at LEGO.com or in the rewards center, are expected on all themes on Insiders Weekend itself, Nov. 21 and 22. Discounts or quadruple points (about 20% back) on selected sets reportedly run Nov. 21 through 26. The specific sets haven't leaked, but they're usually a mix of retiring and recent releases, and retiring sets are already selling out fast. If the rumors hold, Insiders Weekend becomes the better time to buy than Black Friday. Treat the details as unconfirmed for now.

stories.headline: Harley-Davidson finally brings an entry-level bike to the U.S.: the 2027 Sprint 440, assembled in York, Pennsylvania
stories.summary: Harley-Davidson has unveiled the 2027 Sprint 440 for the U.S., the beginner bike critics say it has needed for a decade to compete with Royal Enfield, Triumph, Kawasaki and KTM's 390s. It is the same machine Harley developed with India's Hero MotoCorp and already sells overseas, but final assembly for America will be at Harley's York, Pennsylvania, plant, part of CEO Artie Starrs' "Back to the Bricks" plan to bring work home. It has a 440cc air-cooled single (27 cubic inches) with a six-speed gearbox, a claimed 27 hp and 28 lb-ft, weighs just over 400 pounds wet, and Harley claims 80 mpg from its 2.4-gallon tank. ABS, a 3.5-inch TFT screen and LED lights are standard, and RideApart says the price undercuts every other Harley.

stories.headline: You can now build a 2027 Jeep Wrangler Smoky Mountain online; it starts at $50,545 with eight colors
stories.summary: The 2027 Jeep Wrangler Smoky Mountain Edition, which debuted in Tennessee, is now in Jeep's online Build & Price tool. The four-door special edition is based on the Willys and starts at $50,545, or $52,540 with the $1,995 destination charge. Buyers can choose the standard 2.0-liter turbo four or the 3.6-liter Pentastar V6, which the configurator currently lists at no extra cost, both with an eight-speed automatic. There are eight colors: Bright White and Hydro Blue are free, Joose is $795, and Black, '41, Earl, Firecracker Red and Granite Crystal are $595 each. The hardtop and fender flares are body color, set off by a gloss-black seven-slot grille, smoky black 17-inch wheels and Smoky Mountain hood graphics. A Sky One-Touch power top is optional.

stories.headline: Thieves posing as workers steal two Canon R1s and lenses, about $30,000 of gear, from an F1 photographer in Mexico
stories.summary: An Australian Formula 1 photographer named Ryan lost about $30,000 in gear at the Mexico Grand Prix after leaving his camera bag in the media center for about five minutes on Wednesday, before the center was fully open. When he picked the bag up it felt too light; he first thought friends were pranking him. Security cameras showed two men who appeared to be installing wiring under the desks but were actually going through his bag. They took two Canon EOS R1 bodies and lenses including a 100-300mm, an 85mm and a 14-35mm, and outside cameras caught them running off. Fellow F1 photographer Kym Illman, who shared the story, said tradespeople and flood repairs gave the thieves cover, calling it a "painful reminder about equipment security."

stories.headline: Overnight repaving on Route 111 (Main Street) in Trumbull will start after the polls close on Election Day
stories.summary: The Connecticut Department of Transportation will mill and resurface a short stretch of Route 111 (Main Street) in Trumbull between Whalburn Avenue and Chestnut Hill Road, the town said Friday. To avoid traffic trouble on Election Day, crews from Waters Construction won't start until the polls close on Tuesday, Nov. 3, and will work overnight to finish on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Drivers should expect lane closures on that 0.09-mile segment, with traffic control personnel, signs and local police guiding motorists through the work zone. CTDOT says the schedule could change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions and asks drivers to keep their speed down in the area.
